fields.acceptance: rhiza guide ls lists import as a topic; a testscript checks that rhiza guide import names each of the seven steps in order; the guide size-cap test passes with the new topic.
fields.statement: rhiza guide import prints the procedure for bringing an existing repo with built code into Rhiza: init, survey the repo's code, tests and documents, record built capabilities area by area, bring in load-bearing decisions, retire planning documents into Sources, write unbuilt work as draft change sets, and verify.

fields.acceptance: The import topic states the one-record-per-area rule, the statement and acceptance rules and that anchors come later; a testscript follows those steps on a small fixture repo with tests and gets one landed record change set per area, every capability with a statement and an acceptance naming a test file.
fields.statement: The import procedure records what a repo already does as record change sets, one per area, whose capabilities each state one user-visible behaviour and give as acceptance the repo's existing tests that prove it, without anchors until anchors exist.

fields.acceptance: The import topic states the load-bearing rule and the exact wording form; in a testscript a decision written by that form shows the wording and the Source in rhiza why, and has no quote field.
fields.statement: The import procedure brings in only decisions that shape a capability or constraint, and an imported decision with no owner words has no quote, a wording naming it as the agent's made autonomously and not confirmed by the owner, and a derived-from link to the Source of the document it came from.

fields.acceptance: The import topic names which documents are retired and which are kept; a testscript retires a fixture PLAN.md: rhiza source add with --raw succeeds, the file is deleted in the same commit, and rhiza check passes.
fields.statement: The import procedure retires a planning document by adding it as a Source (a scrubbed summary, the owner's typed words found in it quoted verbatim, the document hashed with --raw) and deleting it in the same change set, and keeps reference, design and operations documents that capabilities link to.

fields.acceptance: The import topic states the rule; a testscript importing a fixture with one unbuilt task and one open question ends with one draft change set naming that Source and one open question, and accepts nothing.
fields.statement: The import procedure writes each unbuilt piece of planned work it finds as a draft intention change set with its intent and the Source it came from, and each open question it finds as a question node, and leaves accepting them to the owner.

fields.acceptance: The import topic states the rule and the question form; a testscript checks the form's example appears in the topic.
fields.statement: The import procedure has the importing agent record every step it could not follow, or had to work around, as a question in the importing repo's model naming the step, so the import can be improved from what it found.
